definition: Behemoth means something of tremendous power or size.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word behemoth. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know behemoth should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The quarry's new excavator was a behemoth, its bucket big enough to cradle a school bus and its treads taller than the foreman.
Giant simply reports unusual size — a giant pumpkin is a happy thing — while behemoth adds monstrous scale and a note of dread.
A juggernaut goes beyond a behemoth: a behemoth overwhelms just by standing there, while a juggernaut is in motion, rolling over rivals and roadblocks alike.

A monstrosity is huge and offensive to look at — the word passes judgment on a thing's appearance, calling it a wrong that should never have been built. A behemoth is dreaded for sheer size and power; it may loom over everything near it, but the word says nothing about ugliness.

A hulk is the bulky shell of something big — often stripped, rusting, or out of service, like a freighter towed to the breakers. It is size without force. A behemoth's size is exactly what makes it powerful, overwhelming everything around it; a hulk merely takes up room.

Behemoth is a whole-word borrowing from Hebrew, the name of the giant beast in the Book of Job. Its root built no other English word, so there is no relative to spot — remember it as a monster's proper name that became a common noun.
Behemoth means something of tremendous power or size.

The city's new stadium rose like a behemoth over the rowhouses of the old neighborhood: ninety thousand seats, parking for a small city of cars, and lights that turned midnight into noon for three blocks in every direction.

Behemoth says more than 'huge': borrowed from the name of a monstrous beast, it carries a shudder — a thing so big it overwhelms everything near it, often with a hint that such size is more menacing than admirable.
Reach for behemoth when size alone is the story and you want a shiver in it — a behemoth of a corporation, a behemoth truck.
Its unit-mate colossus is grand and statuesque, a marvel to look up at; a behemoth looms and crowds.
For a big force on the move, juggernaut adds the momentum.
